title: Runtime mediator for soft model handoff with confidence metrics and attention adaptation
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: We want lower tail latency and cost by attempting low-cost model variants first (speculative decoding) while guaranteeing user-visible correctness and predictable degradation. Current routing/probing artifacts in the runtime do not expose a mediator that makes per-request soft handoff decisions based on calibrated confidence signals and attention profile hints.

Goal: Implement a runtime mediator that sits between prefill and decode stages and performs: (1) light-weight model selection for a given request using kernel and attention fingerprints; (2) continuous acceptance scoring from early tokens to decide whether speculative output can be committed; (3) deterministic, observable fallback to safer model variants or full decode path when acceptance is low or latency SLOs at risk.

Scope: design and implement a mediator component in the serving runtime, server-side telemetry, config knobs for per-customer policies, and safe rollout plan. Also add a small calibration job and evaluation harness to measure acceptance precision/recall on representative prompt sets.

Non-goals: this ticket does not change model weights or add new quantization formats. It will reuse the kernel selection layer and KV cache primitives already tracked in other tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Mediator component integrated into runtime request path and feature-flagged behind runtime-1.20 rollout
Mediator exposes per-request decision logs (model_chosen, acceptance_score, rationale_tags) to observability pipeline

Acceptance metric defined and validated: true_acceptance >= 95% on held-out eval (i.e., speculative outputs accepted should match gold decode in >=95% of cases under configured threshold for low-risk traffic)

Fallback flows exercised end-to-end: (a) immediate fallback to safe model variant, (b) abort speculative commit and re-decode on origin model, (c) degrade to shorter-context fast path with explicit audit log
Latency: median added latency from mediator < 3ms, p95 < 10ms under typical CPU load
Config: per-team policy knobs for acceptance_threshold, latency_budget_ms, cost_priority and model_variant_ordering available in Console
Telemetry: dashboard shows acceptance_rate, false_accept_rate, fallback_rate, cost_per_request, p50/p95 token latency within 24h of rollout
tasks: Design mediator API and lifecycle hooks with runtime and kernel scheduler (design doc)
Implement lightweight fingerprint extractor (attention length, kernel_signature, seq_len_hint) in prefill path
Implement acceptance scorer that runs on first N tokens and emits a probabilistic accept_score
Hook meter into routing layer to trigger speculative decode vs safe path based on policy
Implement safe fallback primitives: re-decode, model-swap with KV cache reconciliation, and audit logging
Add unit + integration tests that simulate race conditions and KV cache mismatches
Add calibration job to run acceptance threshold sweep against eval prompt set and produce recommended default thresholds
Console work: expose policy knobs and realtime metrics for canary customers
Rollout plan: small canary, expanded canary with abort criteria, gradual ramp to 25% and 100%
Postmortem playbook and runbook entries for fallback-induced model divergence
design_decisions: Use a two-stage acceptor: a cheap heuristic pass (kernel+attention fingerprint) followed by a micro-decoders agreement check over 1-4 tokens before committing
Acceptance score is a calibrated float in [0,1] using Platt scaling from offline eval; threshold maps to risk tiers (low/medium/high)
Fallback hierarchy: 1) safe variant same arch and quantization, 2) origin model re-decode with full context, 3) short-context fast path with explicit user warning (customer opt-in)
Kernel selection will prefer kernels that minimize attention copy overhead when early acceptance probability is low, to reduce wasted work on speculative attempts
KV cache reconciliation will be done by keeping speculative cache branches for <= 50 tokens; if rolled back, branch discarded to avoid cache pollution
Audit logging records enough context to correlate acceptance decisions with downstream quality regressions but redacts PII per privacy policy
fallback_plan: If acceptance_score < threshold OR mediator experiences backpressure stalls above latency_budget_ms, immediately trigger fallback according to policy hierarchy. For canary: any false_accept_rate > 1% or p95 latency regression > 10% triggers abort and rollback. Operationally, fallback component supports both synchronous re-decode and async compensating decode (emit speculative result but mark as provisional until re-decode confirms).
telemetry: fallback_rate and fallback_cause breakdown (threshold, latency, error)
latency_ms p50/p95 for mediator stage and for full request
cost_tokens and estimated_cost_delta when speculative path chosen
kernel_mismatch_events (when kernel selection differs between mediator trial and final decode)

risks: Calibration drift: acceptance thresholds may degrade over time as prompts shift; requires periodic re-calibration
Cache divergence: speculative KV branches increase memory pressure and complicate GC if not bounded
Safety/Quality: speculative commits may occasionally surface incorrect or hallucinated content; mitigation requires strict thresholds and stepdown policies
Performance regressions: mediator overhead could erode latency SLOs under heavy load if kernel selection is expensive
